story_type: lifeboat surf training, bow camera in breaking waves
hook: The crew pointed the bow straight at this wave.
narration: A wall of green water rose up in front of the bow, and the crew drove straight into it.
This is Coast Guard Motor Lifeboat 47305 from Station Bodega Bay, in the surf off Dillon Beach, California.
Bodega Bay is one of twenty Coast Guard surf stations. Its crews specialize in rescues in heavy weather and seas.
So on January thirteenth, 2010, they went looking for breaking surf on purpose, to train in it.
Lifeboats like this one are built to roll all the way over and right themselves, with the crew strapped in.
Breaker after breaker buried the bow in white water, then the boat climbed out the other side.
And then the next set came in.
outcome: The lifeboat came out of every breaker upright, and the crew turned back into the surf for another run.
title: Lifeboat drives into a wall of surf
description:
On Jan. 13, 2010, the crew of Motor Lifeboat 47305 from Coast Guard Station Bodega Bay trained in the breaking surf near Dillon Beach in Northern California. The camera rode on the bow.
